We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have guidance: three steps: (1) amide formation from carboxylic acid + amine (coupling). (2) Doebner modification to form α,β-unsaturated acid (alkene) from aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid. (3) sulfonamide formation from amine + sulfonyl chloride.

Thus retrosynthetic direction: target -> break amide to give acid and aniline (or amine). The amide is C(=O)N attached to aniline (c3ccccc3N). So disconnection: amide bond between carbonyl (from acid) and aniline nitrogen. So precursor 1: aromatic aldehyde? Wait amide formation step is forward: acid + amine -> amide. So retrosynthesis: break amide to give carboxylic acid (the α,β-unsaturated acid) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). The acid is part of the unsaturated chain: /C=C/C(=O)N... Actually the amide carbonyl is attached to the alkene chain: /C=C/C(=O)N-aryl. So the acid precursor would be the α,β-unsaturated acid: /C=C/COOH attached to aromatic ring? Let's examine: target fragment: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2 attached to sulfonyl group. The unsaturated acid part is attached to aromatic ring via the alkene: the aromatic ring (c2) has substituent /C=C/C(=O)N... So the acid precursor would be the same but with COOH instead of CONH-aryl. So we need to generate that via Doebner modification: aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid attached to aromatic ring. So the aldehyde precursor would be the aromatic ring with aldehyde at the position where the chain attaches: c2ccc(CHO)cc2 (i.e., p-methyl? Actually the aromatic ring is phenyl with para methyl? The ring is c2ccc(... )cc2 attached to sulfonyl group. The substituent is at para position relative to sulfonyl? Not needed.

Thus step 2: from aromatic aldehyde (p-substituted phenyl) + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid (cinnamic acid derivative). So we need to identify the aldehyde: c2ccc(C=O)cc2 (para to sulfonyl). So precursor 2: p-methyl? Wait the ring also has methyl at position 1 (the outer ring). The outer ring is Cc1ccc(... )cc1 (toluene). So the sulfonamide attaches to that outer ring. The inner ring (c2) is attached to sulfonyl and has the unsaturated chain. So the aldehyde is on that inner ring.

Thus step 3: sulfonamide formation: from sulfonyl chloride (Ar-SO2Cl) reacting with aniline (the outer ring amine). So we need sulfonyl chloride precursor: the sulfonyl chloride attached to inner phenyl (c2) with the unsaturated acid substituent. So precursor 3: Ar-SO2Cl (where Ar is the inner phenyl with the unsaturated acid). So we need to generate that sulfonyl chloride from the sulfonamide product by breaking S-N bond.

Thus overall retrosynthesis:

Target (T) -> break amide: gives unsaturated acid (A) + aniline (B). (Step 1: amide formation forward, retrosynthesis break amide.)

A is α,β-unsaturated acid attached to phenyl (c2). This can be derived via Doebner modification from aromatic aldehyde (C) + malonic acid (common). So break C=C bond to give aldehyde (C) and malonic acid (common). (Step 2.)

B (aniline) is attached to outer phenyl (toluene). The sulfonamide formation step: break S-N bond to give sulfonyl chloride (D) attached to inner phenyl with unsaturated acid, and aniline (outer phenyl). So D is sulfonyl chloride.

Thus we need to propose three reactions with template IDs. We need to find appropriate template IDs for each transformation.

We can search for amide formation template (carboxylic acid + amine -> amide). Use functional_groups_broken: aliphatic carboxylic acid; formed: amide. Already attempted but got empty. Maybe need to specify functional_groups_broken: ["aliphatic carboxylic acid"] and formed: ["amide"]. It returned empty earlier. Could be that template exists but not returned due to limit? Let's try search without specifying formed.
